name: Crispus
overview: Crispus is a male figure noted in the New Testament as the believing leader of the synagogue in Corinth. His role as a synagogue leader highlights his prominence within the early Christian community in that city. Beyond this, no additional personal or tribal details are recorded.
namesAndTitles: The name 'Crispus' is the only name associated with this individual in Scripture, and no specific meaning or divine origin is provided. Another name, 'Sosthenes,' appears in the same chapter but refers to a different person and is not directly connected to Crispus.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Crispus beyond his leadership position in the Corinthian synagogue. There are no listed relatives or other personal connections documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Crispus is significant as a prominent early convert to Christianity, exemplified by his leadership role in the synagogue at Corinth. His belief and acceptance of the gospel represent the transformative impact of the Christian message within established Jewish communities. His mention underscores the early church's growth and the inclusion of influential Jewish leaders among the believers.
